title: Strange Horses
subtitle: The walking man, the crouching animal. In the blink of an eye, in a fleeting moment.

items.text: The spring scenery of the steppes stretches out to the edge of the horizon.
The expedition team continues to trek in the direction indicated by the river.
As they do, they scarcely notice as the terrain beneath them changes. Until the party at last finds themselves walking across bare rock.

The uneven green rocks merge with grayish and purple granite, rough and jagged. In spots, tumbleweed and sand rice plants pierce through the jagged stone, billowing and cascading, and then plummeting down the cliff.
The travelers also feel as though they are moving downward. As the surrounding peculiarities increase, so too does their breathing, which becomes increasingly restricted.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: *pants*

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: You proved yourself right by ... finding running water for us ...

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: So, I'm not ... judging you ... this time, but ...

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: Are we going the wrong way?

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: No. This is the right direction.

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: But it's getting harder and harder to breathe, even if we are going down the mountain.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: What about you, Madam? Are you feeling alright?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I feel fine. Perhaps because I'm used to climbing mountains.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: But we are definitely 3000 meters above the sea level now. It's normal if you're feeling unwell at this height. If only we still had alcohol ...

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Well, it's just a thought. I wouldn't have gathered enough courage to climb up that slope if I hadn't taken the last few sips.
Bessmert shakes her head, dispelling unnecessary thoughts, and instead pursues another possibility.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: But, child, are you sure we are on the right path?

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: I don't think it's wrong. The clearer the sign, the higher the accuracy.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: And the sign I just saw happened to be exceptionally clear.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: What about the others? Are you feeling alright? Shall we stop and take a short break?

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: I have a bad feeling. Instead of a break, we need a new direction. Back home, for example.

items.speaker: Jurien
items.text: Before we do anything, can we have some rest? My head has been pounding for a while. I thought it was common in the mountains and you all felt the same.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Yes, headache is a common altitude sickness, Sir.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Wait, is that tumbleweed?! I don't think it belongs here.
Yenisei finally notices a large bundle trundling on not far away.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: I hear ... Are they rolling nearby? Are you sure?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: This is not the right season for them to roll and spread seeds.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: I'm not seeing things, I guess, but I don't know why they are here. And those flowers ...
The team members at the end of their procession stop in their tracks. The others beside him also stop as a result.
Until the entire team comes to a standstill.

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: Something's wrong.

items.speaker: Team Member II
items.text: Hey you ... where are you taking us?

items.speaker: Team Member II
items.text: Haven't you noticed the rocks around us? Their color is abnormal. I've never seen anything like this, not even in books ...

items.speaker: Team Member II
items.text: And look at the holes in the rocks! They were made by water erosion! And that's not supposed to happen in this climate!

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Calm down, Sir. Perhaps we have reached somewhere beyond other adventurers' records, but that's all ...

items.speaker: Team Member II
items.text: What about this?! How are you going to explain it?!

items.speaker: Team Member II
items.text: Another one of your stupid arcane skill tricks?
Yenisei lowers her head to look at what seem to be ordinary yellow flowers.
But these flowers wither almost immediately after blooming. It would be difficult to describe such a scene as anything less than a miracle or a curse.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: What? This is ...

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: What is it? Explain what?

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: I don't know what species it is. It looks like a mini sunflower, but ...

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: Told you we should head back. Something's wrong with this dump.

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: Agree. We have a situation now. We should go back while we still can.

items.speaker: Jurien
items.text: Ladies, I have to say this is beyond my imagination.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: It's just a flower, yes? Why are you all so scared? I can't see, but ...

Bessmert reaches out to grasp the flowers again, but the petals wither beneath her fingertips. Now more puzzled, she tries touching a complete cluster, but only ends up with a handful of withered husks.
The scent of these withered fragments turns rotten as their sweet fragrance disappears, leaving her having captured only the base note of their "perfume."

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Emm? The smell ...

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: Everything is wrong here. The fog is not supposed to form at this latitude, the terrain is strange, and the plants … they wither in an instant!

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: I don't want to say this, but this place seems to be cursed.

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: These phenomena make no sense. We have to go back now.
The voice of the young man is more resolute than ever before.
Faced with such a bizarre situation, escape is unarguably the most rational choice.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: You heard them, Madam. What do you say? Things are indeed weird.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: No, we are not returning. We have made it through the thunderstorm. What could be more dangerous than that?

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Perhaps we are getting close, like those merchants said, there will be a "price" we must pay for the Ask and Acquire. Mr. Jurien, you also asked me about it, don't you remember?

items.speaker: Jurien
items.text: On the contrary, Madam, I remember it clearly. I have also told you my suspicion—it could be an exchange made between the arcanists and nature.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: What? Of course not.

items.speaker: Jurien
items.text: Look around you—all these bizarre phenomena! You know I wasn't making things up. You set out to pursue that arcane skill, yet we ended up here ...

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: I don't know what your next plan is, but count me out.
Agitated by this abnormal phenomenon and talk of a possible sacrifice, the young man pushes Bessmert aside and stands with the others at the back of the group.
A previous scene of division and opposition repeats itself.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: No, I swear on my life, that is not my intention!

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Madam Bessmert would never do that.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: The point is, the compass doesn't work here. You will get lost on the way back without me.

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: There's no doubt this is part of your scheme.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Excuse me?

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: Mr. Jurien already told us about your secret arcane skill. It's our last hope of getting home in this plight.

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: We trust him. That being the case, you must come with us.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: No. I came here with Madam Bessmert. I'm not leaving without her.
Yenisei also expresses her intentions clearly. Never having been one to be swayed by external forces, unless ...

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Let's ...

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: It's fine, Madam. We can keep going on our own ...

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: Let's go back.
… Unless the person she is supporting lowers her head first.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: It's alright. Though I can't see, I can imagine how shocking it must be to make you so uneasy.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: When we get back to the pastureland ...

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: I'm sorry, Madam. We are not taking you.

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: I don't think we have enough supplies for everyone to make it back, so certainly someone must be abandoned.
Yenisei takes a step closer until she is completely blocking the depressed Bessmert's path.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: Then, allow me to say no. I will not show you the way without Madam Bessmert in the team.

items.speaker: Bessmert
items.text: No, Yeni. You're going with them.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: But they are leaving you behind!

items.speaker: Krolik
items.text: Looks like your assistant has made her own decision. Sorry, but I never thought it would end up like this ...

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: Enough with the talking. My apologies, ladies.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: What ... What are you doing?!
They are now facing each other, seeming to have decided to end their dispute through force.
They are acutely aware that sacrificing one might save the many.
It is a simple matter of arithmetic.
Standing upright is a phenomenon exclusive to humans. It is a miracle born of a desire to break free from the earth and move upward towards the sky.
The outcome unfolds quite apart from everyone's expectations.

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Striped Horse?
items.text: *neighs*

items.speaker: Yenisei
items.text: I-I don't understand. What is ... What is going on?!
Even though they acknowledge the untimely nature of their dispute, they are left to witness all hope of reconciliation disintegrate before them.
Yenisei receives no answer, as the people standing in front of her now have lost the ability to reply.
